units.translation: And I am ashamed to say
What must one do or say to win the favor of the gods?
Speak, instruct me
Such a fortress I tell you this is
Speak
I say what I wish
And I include you among these
I seem to be speaking much and in vain
He does not seem to speak untimely
To speak what is fitting
He says that a great Achaean assault was made by night
And I hope to speak in common
Am I speaking to a deaf person?
You would speak as quickly as possible
Nor do I speak from (this is corrupted from 'waters') Ismenus
I would speak knowing well the affairs of the enemy
This night which you speak of, gleaming with stars on a shield, belongs to heaven
Speak of another assigned to other gates
I will tell of the one who drew the lot for the gates
Do not begrudge me by speaking
And the fifth I say
To this one whom you call the Arcadian
The sixth I would say is a most prudent man
He speaks this word through his mouth
A fine thing to hear and to say for those who are drunk
The seventh indeed - I will tell
As the letters say
Saying that gain comes before later doom
One might speak of what one has accomplished
For I speak of an ancient transgression swiftly avenged
You speak of a piercing [blow]
To speak double
To speak destructive things
Thus it has been commanded to speak about this
But I speak to the leaders of the Cadmeans
And I will tell you
And these things I say I saw at night
You speak terrible things
You say that he is carried off dead
The suffering that one can neither speak nor ask about
Speak, having taken your stand
He said these things to your son Xerxes
So much he said
Speak
I omit many things in speaking
I revere to speak against
Not a lengthy speech, but a concise one, speaking
Having spoken things hard to say to friends
Tell me something clear
They say that you acquired great wealth for your children
How did you say these things?
You speak of evils before evils for the noble Persians
Speaking hateful things before evils
What do you say has been saved?
He would speak most clearly
Of these things you might speak (thus Hartung for 'speak') whatever is possible
To say nothing
Or do I speak clearly?
I speak of the light of this night that has now given birth
Such a proof and token I give you
And I would like to hear these words again, which you speak
You speak prudent things kindly
They groan, speaking well of the man
He will utter the word of joy rather than speaking
You say that the army longs for this land, longing for it
One might say that some things are easy to bear
For if I were to speak of the toils
And if one were to speak of the storm
Why should one speak of those who perished in the vote?
Why need you tell me the greater things?
There is no way I would call false things good
I do not speak falsely
For how do you say that a storm came upon the naval army?
It is fitting to sing a paean of the Erinyes
Saying that the storm of the Achaeans was not without the wrath of the gods
They say that we are destroyed
I would say that he went to the city of Ilium
I would speak knowing
Whether I speak of him dead or alive
I will not be ashamed to speak to you of my husband-loving ways
I will tell of my own hard-to-bear life
He is wounded more than a net, so to speak
For I do not speak of the land below
I would say this man
Speaking to you, she ceases her clear speech
Speaking within her mind, I persuade her with words
